Shattered Legacy's own art for TazUO, shipped in the player package (cc-P26, F-8)
================================================================================

What is here
------------
  art\<id>.png    art overrides, by static item ID in decimal. The build copies them to
                  app\tazuo\ExternalImages\art\, where TazUO draws them instead of the art in the
                  player's artLegacyMUL.uop (TazUO ExternalImageLoader.Load and Art.LoadSourceArtInfo).
  registry.csv    every art ID we use, one row each. scripts\find-free-art.py reads it so a later pack
                  never takes one of these IDs.
  records.json    our tiledata and animdata records for the IDs that need them. The build copies it to
                  app\art-records.json. Play.ps1 writes it into copies of the player's own
                  tiledata.mul and animdata.mul (app\uo-overrides\), never into the player's EA files.
                  Nothing of EA's is shipped: not a file, not a part of one.

Shattered runestone (IDs 15376-15419, 0x3C10-0x3C3B)
----------------------------------------------------
Author:      Vrark
Resource:    "Animated Runestone", https://www.servuo.dev/archive/animated-runestone.2564/
             Posted 2025-12-27. Its description in full: "An animated runestone in four directions."
Downloaded:  2026-09-30, by Chase (logged in to servuo.dev). Original download kept at
             D:\UO\third-party\animated-runestone\ ("MMH7 runestone.zip": four GIFs and four zips of PNGs).
License:     NO LICENSE STATED, in the download or on the page. Posted for the ServUO community to use.
             The download's folder and file names ("MMH7 runestone", "MM7H runestone 2") are a
             misnaming, not a sign of where the art came from. Cleared for use, and to ship to
             players, by Chase on 2026-10-02 ("the art is fine just missnamed"; shard-migration
             notes\p26-decisions-2026-10-02.md, item 1).

The four "designs" are Vrark's four directions of the one stone:
  design 1  15376-15386  Test1_0001_top.png .. Test1_0011_top.png  (MMH7 runestone 1.zip)
  design 2  15387-15397  Test2_0001_top.png .. Test2_0011_top.png  (MM7H runestone 2.zip, folder TOP\)
  design 3  15398-15408  Test3_0001_top.png .. Test3_0011_top.png  (MMH7 runestone 3.zip)
  design 4  15409-15419  Test4_0001_top.png .. Test4_0011_top.png  (MMH7 runestone 4.zip)
Each base ID (the first of each run) is the item's ID and the only one with records. The other ten
are frames only.

Changed from the download, and only this: each design's frames were cut to the union of their
non-transparent pixels (the same cut for all 11, so they stay registered), then given 22 transparent
rows below. That puts the floating stone over the centre of its tile; TazUO puts an image's bottom row
on the tile's bottom tip and its middle column on the tile's centre. No pixel was scaled or altered:
scripts\anchor-art-frames.py checks every frame it writes against its source, pixel for pixel. Before
that, the 44 PNGs were checked byte-identical to the ones in Vrark's four zips.

  python scripts\anchor-art-frames.py --src D:\UO\third-party\animated-runestone\frames\stone<N>
      --first-id <base> --out player-package\vendor\shattered-legacy-art\art --bottom-pad 22

Frame timing: the GIFs run 80 to 90 ms a frame. TazUO's static animation step is
FrameInterval x 100 ms (AnimatedStaticsManager.Process, ITEM_EFFECT_ANIMATION_DELAY 50, doubled), so
records.json uses interval 1: about 100 ms a frame, a little slower than the GIFs.

Tiledata record: copied from OSI's own animated runestone, 0xADBA "Runestone01 Glow01", as read from
the client's tiledata.mul on 2026-10-01: flags 0x01040040 (Animation, PartialHue, Impassable),
weight 1, height 3. Only the name ("shattered runestone") is ours. The flag values are facts about how
OSI's item behaves, not EA data shipped: the record is written by hand here.
